growth_story.headline: Aid lifted income per person to a 2013 peak; it drifted down as aid fell, collapsed in 2021 and is now about where it was in 2006.
growth_story.arc: From 2001 to 2013, Afghanistan's income per person grew 5.3 percent a year on average, as civilian and security grants drove fast growth in services. Growth swung widely from year to year, with jumps such as 22.0 percent in 2002 and 17.0 percent in 2009, and farm output depended heavily on the weather. From 2014 to 2024 the average was -3.7 percent a year: grants shrank, insecurity spread and disputed elections hurt confidence, so income per person slipped a little in most years up to 2019. The collapse came after the August 2021 political crisis, when international aid stopped suddenly and income per person fell 22.6 percent in 2021 and another 7.6 percent in 2022. It was flat in 2023 and fell 1.0 percent in 2024, while large numbers of Afghans returned from Iran and Pakistan, leaving it 35.5 percent below the 2013 peak and about where it first was in 2006.

threads.title: Aid built a services boom
threads.text: After 2001, civilian and security grants poured in and the service economy grew fast. Farm output grew quickly too but swung with the weather, so growth rose and fell sharply from year to year.

citations.title: Policy Notes: Priorities for Inclusive Development in Afghanistan
citations.quote: Civilian and security grant inflows spurred rapid expansion of the service economy, which experienced consistent double-digit growth.

citations.title: Policy Notes: Priorities for Inclusive Development in Afghanistan

threads.title: Shrinking aid and rising insecurity
threads.text: International grants declined rapidly after 2011, fighting intensified, and disputed presidential elections in 2014 and 2019 harmed confidence. Income per person stopped rising and slipped slightly in most years between 2014 and 2019.

citations.title: Policy Notes: Priorities for Inclusive Development in Afghanistan
citations.quote: Insecurity has intensified, and the disputed outcomes of the 2014 and 2019 presidential elections have harmed confidence.

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update October 2022: Adjusting to the New Realities
citations.quote: Reflecting decreased grant support and heightened political instability, real growth in the gross domestic product (GDP) declined

threads.title: The 2021 aid stop
threads.text: After the August 2021 political crisis, international aid stopped suddenly, civil servants went unpaid, development spending ended and a crisis of confidence hit banks and firms. Income per person fell 22.6 percent in 2021 and 7.6 percent in 2022, and the economy settled at a much lower level of demand.

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update October 2022: Adjusting to the New Realities
citations.quote: The sudden stop of international aid and the confidence crisis culminated in three inter-related simultaneous shocks.

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update October 2022: Adjusting to the New Realities
citations.quote: civil servants stopped receiving their salaries, development spending ended abruptly, and basic public services were disrupted.

citations.title: Afghanistan's Contracted Economy Faces Uncertainty, Afghan Families Are Struggling

threads.title: Returnees outpace output
threads.text: Since September 2023, millions of Afghans have returned from Iran and Pakistan. Their demand lifts services and industry, but the population is growing faster than output, so income per person keeps falling.

threads.title: Women shut out of work
threads.text: Restrictions imposed by the Taliban administration on women's education and work hold back the country's human capital. The World Bank said in 2023, and again in 2025, that they lower growth prospects.

since_last_year.text: In the Afghan fiscal year to March 2026, returns from Iran and Pakistan peaked in mid-2025, and the World Bank estimates that population growth outpaced output, so income per person fell again. Aid kept falling, drought cut farm output, and the border with Pakistan has been closed since October 2025, pushing trade onto other routes through Iran and Central Asia.

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update
citations.quote: However, rapid population growth has outpaced economic expansion, leading to falling incomes per person.

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update
citations.quote: A sharp decline in foreign aid, successive natural disasters —including drought and earthquakes—and the prolonged Afghanistan–Pakistan border closure since October 2025

citations.title: Afghanistan Development Update
citations.quote: agricultural output contracted in FY2025 due to drought conditions, despite relatively resilient performance in irrigated wheat.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank describes an economy that grew in 2024 and 2025, but in the data income per person was flat in 2023 at 0.1 percent and fell 1.0 percent in 2024. The sources put the gap down to people: returnees made the population grow faster than output, so a growing economy still meant falling income per person.
